decisions.executionNote: Turn both wrists toward the table along gradual elbow-up approach arcs; inspect new layout before selecting peg assignments.
Align left over the near blue block and right over the lone star, with vertical approaches and open grippers.
Close on the aligned blue block and star, then lift vertically to verify retention visually.
Both pieces appear retained. Raise for clearance, carry blue to the second peg and the single star to the shortest rightmost peg; maintain separated workspaces.
Use wrist views to compensate off-center grasps, approaching the blue and star pegs slowly. Hold closed until insertion is visually established.
Separate the wrists to avoid mutual interference, then refine the star alignment over the shortest peg while keeping the blue piece lifted.
Seat and release the star on the shortest peg, then lift the right gripper to inspect insertion; left continues holding the blue block clear.
Star remains on its peg after release. Clear the right arm outward and align the held blue piece over the second peg before a slow descent.
Lower blue along the visible peg, release and inspect. Move the cleared right gripper above the remaining right-side blue piece.
Clear the inserted blue piece and approach the other two blue blocks in each arm's own workspace, adjusting yaw to their long axes.
Refine blue-block alignment from wrist views. Grasp and lift the right block while lowering the left gripper toward the remaining left block.
Lift the left blue block for placement. Bring the retained right blue toward a central staging area, keeping the arms separated.
Bring the centered second blue block over its peg, rotating into alignment; keep the other held block clear while checking the insertion geometry.
The second blue block appears tilted against the peg. Lift to relieve contact and shift slightly toward the peg before another insertion attempt; prior placements still need verification.
Stage the blue pieces away from the base to recover a flat, centered grasp. The tilted left piece should not be forced down onto the peg.
Release the staged blue pieces near the tabletop and lift open grippers so their resting orientation and the base can be assessed.
Approach the now-flat left blue block at its center. Bring the right wrist above the star to verify and, if needed, correct its seating.
Regrasp and vertically lift the flat left blue block. The star visibly surrounds its peg, so leave it undisturbed and clear the right arm toward its staged blue.
Carry the recovered blue block above its peg, preserving the grasp; lower the right gripper toward its staged block while keeping it outside the placement area.
Use a short, slow descent to compare blue-hole alignment before contact; center and regrasp the staged right blue piece, then lift it clear.
Relieve the contact and correct the held blue toward the far side of the base; the wrist view indicates a substantial fore-aft hole mismatch.
Continue the measured visual-servo correction toward the blue peg with a small diagonal descent, keeping the other block stationary.
Make the final small fore-aft correction and descend gradually to check whether the peg enters the held blue hole without tilting the piece.
Reset the approach using head-camera geometry rather than the displaced blue piece as a reference; lift and realign above the second peg.
Descend vertically over the calibrated second-peg position in small increments; inspect contact before release instead of following the displaced block.
The previously perched blue has moved off the peg. Lift the held block away from contact, compensate its shifted grasp, and approach the now-visible peg again.
Release the unstable left grasp and withdraw leftward. Bring the flat right-held blue toward the shared central peg only after the left arm clears, keeping the arms uncrossed.
Replan with smaller increments after the continuity rejection. Keep the left arm clear and align the flat right-held blue using its observed hole offset before lowering.
Correct the right block laterally onto the exposed second peg, then release near base height. Approach a red disk with the left arm while keeping the placement area clear.
Withdraw the open right gripper to inspect the newly aligned blue block. Center the left gripper on the red disk, close and lift to verify retention.
Carry the centered red disk toward the two-piece peg at clearance height. Approach a right-side yellow piece with the free arm, keeping separate motion corridors.
Align the red hole over the third peg at clearance height. Square the right gripper to the yellow piece before closing, then begin lifting outward.
Lower the centered red disk toward the exposed third peg for a close alignment check. Move the retained yellow outward and upward so the wrists cannot interfere.
Seat and release the red disk, then lift to verify it remains on the peg. Carry yellow through the right-front corridor to a central staging point for a non-crossing transfer.

After the guard interruption, separate the wrists first: withdraw the open left arm leftward and lift while the right moves into the front corridor, then continue the yellow staging approach with smaller increments.
Approach the final red disk with the left arm. Lower the right-held yellow onto a front-center staging spot for later pickup after the right arm withdraws.
Center and grasp the remaining red disk, then lift. Release the yellow at the staging spot and withdraw the right arm fully before any left-side transfer.
Hold red clear on the left while the right approaches the misplaced blue obstructing the red peg. Clear that obstruction before another insertion.
Close on the obstructing blue at the observed head-view location and lift before moving aside; verify retention rather than assuming the blocked aperture is a grasp.
The attempted blue grasp was empty; clear the right arm completely. Bring the retained red directly above the now-exposed third peg for isolated visual alignment.
Make a small fore-aft correction while lowering the retained red toward the exposed peg, with the other arm stationary and clear.
The red hole now visibly surrounds the peg tip. Lower a little farther with a small centering adjustment, then open without lateral withdrawal.
Lift away from the red placement before moving toward the displaced red disk. Approach the remaining far-right yellow in the separate right workspace.
Regrasp the displaced red at its observed center. Lift the far yellow and carry it through the right-side clearance corridor toward staging.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion. Lift and check red retention; carry the yellow toward a separate front staging spot.
The red was not retained. Reopen and approach with corrected fore-aft centering. Replan the yellow staging move at smaller increments after the joint-continuity rejection.
The red is now centered between the fingers. Close and lift vertically to verify retention; release the staged yellow and withdraw the right arm.
Carry the retained red over its peg, accounting for the more centered new grasp. Keep the right arm outside the insertion workspace.
Continue the isolated red insertion slowly, keeping the hole centered on the visible white tip and retaining the grasp until the seating geometry is clearer.
Center the red hole a few millimeters over the visible peg, release without lateral motion, and lift slightly to inspect whether it remains engaged.
Recenter the partially engaged red disk a few millimeters toward the visible peg axis, lower gently, and release again without pushing the surrounding pieces.
Clear the left arm before bringing the right wrist over the lone star to inspect its peg engagement and recover any perched placement.
Leave the red and star peg engagement undisturbed. Clear the right arm and align the left gripper to recover the loose diagonal blue obstructing the left peg area.
Center the left fingers on the loose blue using the rotated wrist view, close, then lift vertically before translating it toward its own peg.
The last grasp was empty, while a blue now visibly surrounds its peg. Leave that piece alone and approach the loose rear blue with a lower, centered grasp.
Tracking was interrupted near the pegs. Replan from the observed pose and lift the open left gripper clear before any further rotation or descent.
The prior chunk executed nothing. Use a smaller clearance lift with a slight left-forward correction to preserve joint-target continuity.
The star appears offset from its exposed peg rather than seated. Clear the left arm and approach the star itself for a controlled regrasp and measured correction.
Lift the open right fingers clear so the star can settle, then center the wrist for inspection. Approach an unobstructed left-side yellow with a vertical, elbow-up grasp.
Move the open right gripper laterally clear of the tilted star so it can settle. Center and grasp the left yellow, then lift for retention verification.
Bring the retained yellow above the tall left peg with extra clearance. Approach the now-flat star from above with the right gripper open.
Lower yellow toward its peg with an offset correction from the head view. Center and close on the settled star, then lift only enough to verify a stable grasp.
Continue the yellow insertion with a small lateral centering correction. Raise and align the retained star above its own peg while maintaining wrist separation.
